ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The left/center of the figure is an iodonium-ion-like three-membered ring structure, the iodine atom is labeled I+, and is connected to two adjacent carbon atoms in the form of dashed/partial bonds; these two ring carbons each are connected to two methyl groups, so it is a tetramethyl-substituted C-C unit. At the lower right there is a separate AcO−, indicating an acetate anion. The curved arrows in the figure indicate electron movement, and the problem asks to ignore the arrows. Then reason: The separate acetate anion can be written as CC(=O)[O-]. The positively charged cyclic iodonium fragment is a C-I-C three-membered ring, and the two ring carbons each bear two methyl groups, so it can be encoded as CC1(C)[I+]C1(C)C. The two fragments are not connected and are connected with a dot, therefore the SMILES is CC(=O)[O-].CC1(C)[I+]C1(C)C.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: it shows a separate AcO− group and a positively charged iodine-containing three-membered ring attached to a tetramethyl-substituted C-C unit, with curved arrows that should not be included. Convert the acetate counterion to CC(=O)[O-]. Then encode the cyclic iodonium fragment by starting at one methyl-substituted ring carbon, adding its extra methyl branch, bonding to [I+], continuing to the second methyl-substituted ring carbon, and closing the ring back to the first carbon while adding the remaining methyl branches. Combine the disconnected fragments with a dot to obtain CC(=O)[O-].CC1(C)[I+]C1(C)C.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct visual-to-SMILES transcription: identify the two disconnected species and encode their connectivity/charges rather than using reaction-arrow meaning.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the drawing as a charged ion pair: a separate acetate anion labeled OAc with a minus sign, and a cyclic iodonium structure in which iodine is positively charged and bridges the two carbons of a three-membered ring. Each of the two ring carbons bears two methyl substituents, and curved arrows are explicitly ignored.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction to choose the SMILES for the transition-state structure and specifically to ignore the arrows, so only atoms, bonds, charges, and disconnected components in the image are encoded.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use organic SMILES conventions: dot separates disconnected ions; acetate anion is written as CC(=O)[O-]; positively charged iodine is [I+]; ring closure digits encode the C-I-C three-membered ring; methyl substituents on the ring carbons are written as branches.
